`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

seats.text:
The room reached unanimous consensus on the program's output, matching my independently verified answer, and `answer.txt` has been written with:

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

The trickiest part of the trace was the `DEF shadow` procedure: `SET total 5` creates a local, `GLOBAL total` then binds `total` to the global for the rest of the call, so the subsequent `PRINT total` reads the pre-existing global (101), and only then does `SET total 7` update the global before returning.

seats.text:
The room reached unanimous consensus on:

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

This matches what I wrote to `answer.txt`. Key trace points: `total`'s value diverges between global/local across `addup`/`bump`/`tick` due to `GLOBAL` scoping rules; `DEF shadow` has an internal `PRINT total` (printing global 101) before its `RET`; `fact 20` and `POW 2 100` are large bignums verified with Python; and `CALL early`/`CALL inner` before their `DEF` yield 0 per the "undefined call yields 0" rule.
